issues.legal_issue: A co-owner of acquired land is entitled to the enhanced compensation awarded to other co-owners for the same land, even when the co-owner’s own reference claim was rejected as time-barred.
material_facts: The claimant and her children jointly owned the acquired land.
The children obtained enhanced compensation in a land reference.
The claimant’s own reference was rejected because it had been made late.
The Land Acquisition Collector later granted the claimant the enhancement awarded to the children, and the appeal challenged that grant.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the grant of enhanced compensation to the claimant and dismissed the appeal. It did not decide whether Section 28A applied.
issues.legal_principle: On first principles, one co-owner is entitled to the benefit of enhanced compensation awarded to other co-owners in a reference concerning jointly owned acquired land. The Court relied in support on A. Vishwanath Pillai v. Special Tehsildar for Land Acquisition, AIR 1991 SC 1966. It found it unnecessary to decide the applicability of Section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

predicates.compensation_redetermination_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision that grants a claimant enhanced compensation by reference to an award for other claimants.
predicates.claimant_is_joint_owner: The claimant jointly owns the acquired land with the other claimants.
predicates.co_owners_obtained_enhancement_for_same_: Other co-owners obtained enhanced compensation in a reference concerning the same jointly owned acquired land.
predicates.claimant_reference_was_rejected_as_time_: The claimant’s own request for a reference was rejected because it was made late.
predicates.claimant_receives_same_enhancement: The claimant receives the enhancement awarded to the other co-owners.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges enhanced compensation granted to a joint owner, and the other joint owners obtained enhancement for the same land while the claimant’s own reference was rejected as late, the claimant receives that same enhancement.
